subject: science
prompt_en: Golu says: 'Vegetarians can't get protein, because protein is only in meat and eggs.' Correct him.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Vegetarian logon ko protein nahi milta, kyonki protein sirf meat aur ande mein hota hai.' Use sahi karo.
answer: Plant foods like dal, rajma, chana, soybean and peanuts, and dairy foods like milk, paneer and curd, all give protein.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin what the different nutrients in food do, using foods from your kitchen.
prompt_hi: Apne chhote cousin ko samjhao ki khaane ke alag-alag poshak tatva kya karte hain, apne kitchen ke khaane ke example se.
answer: Key ideas: carbohydrates (roti, rice) and fats (ghee, oil) give energy; proteins (dal, milk) build and repair the body; vitamins and minerals (fruits, vegetables) protect us; fibre helps digestion; water is needed for everything.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: what is roughage, and why do we need it?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: roughage kya hai, aur hume iski zaroorat kyon hai?
answer: Roughage is dietary fibre, the part of plant food we cannot digest; it helps food move through the gut and prevents constipation.

subject: science
prompt_en: How can you test a groundnut for fat using just a piece of paper? (Don't eat the groundnut you tested, and skip this one if anyone nearby has a peanut allergy.)
prompt_hi: Sirf ek kaagaz se moongphali mein fat hai ya nahi, kaise test karoge? (Test ki hui moongphali khaana nahi, aur agar kisi ko moongphali se allergy hai toh yeh test mat karna.)
answer: Crush and rub the groundnut on the paper and let it dry; an oily, translucent patch that lets light through and does not dry away shows fat. Do not eat the tested groundnut; avoid it if anyone has a peanut allergy.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: your teacher puts a drop of dilute iodine on a cut potato and on a slice of cucumber. What will you see on each?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: teacher kate hue aloo aur kheere ke tukde pe patle iodine ki ek boond daalti hain. Dono pe kya dikhega?
answer: The potato turns blue-black (it has starch); the cucumber shows little or no blue-black and stays the brownish-yellow colour of iodine (very little starch).

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: the teacher adds iodine to sugar solution and to rice water (the starchy water from cooking rice). Which turns blue-black?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: teacher cheeni ke ghol aur chawal ke maand mein iodine daalti hain. Kaunsa neela-kaala hoga?
answer: Only the rice water. Iodine shows starch; sugar is a carbohydrate but not starch, so it does not turn blue-black.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict which ones (there may be more than one) leave a patch on paper that stays even after drying: a drop of water, a drop of coconut oil, or crushed coconut.
prompt_hi: Guess karo, inme se kaun kaun (ek se zyada bhi ho sakte hain) kaagaz pe aisa daag chhodenge jo sookhne ke baad bhi rahe: paani ki boond, nariyal tel ki boond, ya pisa hua nariyal?
answer: The coconut oil and the crushed coconut (both contain fat); the water patch dries and disappears.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why do we wait for the paper to dry before deciding that a food has fat?
prompt_hi: Kisi khaane mein fat hai, ye decide karne se pehle kaagaz ke sookhne ka intezaar kyon karte hain?
answer: Water also makes a wet patch, but it dries and disappears; only an oily patch stays translucent after drying.

subject: science
prompt_en: Milk and rice water both look white. The teacher tests both with iodine and with the protein test. What results would you expect?
prompt_hi: Doodh aur chawal ka maand dono safed dikhte hain. Teacher dono ko iodine aur protein test se jaanchti hain. Kya result expect karoge?
answer: Rice water turns blue-black with iodine (starch). Milk does not turn blue-black with iodine, but it turns violet in the protein test.

subject: science
prompt_en: In the lab, your teacher tests a piece of paneer: iodine shows no blue-black, the paper shows an oily patch, and the protein test turns violet. What nutrients does paneer have?
prompt_hi: Lab mein teacher ne paneer ka tukda test kiya: iodine se neela-kaala nahi hua, kaagaz pe tel ka daag aaya, aur protein test baingani hua. Paneer mein kaun se poshak tatva hain?
answer: Fat and protein (and little or no starch).

subject: science
prompt_en: A packet of chips says 'no added fat'. How could you check with a paper test whether the chips still have oil in them?
prompt_hi: Chips ke packet pe likha hai 'no added fat'. Kaagaz wale test se kaise check karoge ki chips mein ab bhi tel hai ya nahi?
answer: Crush a chip and rub it on paper, let it dry, and hold it to the light; an oily translucent patch that stays means the chips contain fat.

subject: science
prompt_en: Here are lab results in words: potato turned blue-black with iodine; groundnut gave an oily patch and turned violet; egg white turned violet only. Make a table with columns starch, fat and protein and fill in ✓ or ✗ from these results.
prompt_hi: Lab ke results shabdon mein: aloo iodine se neela-kaala hua; moongphali ne tel ka daag diya aur baingani hui; ande ki safedi sirf baingani hui. Starch, fat aur protein ke columns wali table banao aur in results se ✓ ya ✗ bharo.
answer: Potato: starch ✓, fat ✗, protein ✗. Groundnut: starch ✗, fat ✓, protein ✓. Egg white: starch ✗, fat ✗, protein ✓.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu's notebook says: 'Groundnut gave an oily patch, so groundnut has only fat. No need for the protein test.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu ki notebook mein likha hai: 'Moongphali ne tel ka daag diya, matlab moongphali mein sirf fat hai. Protein test ki zaroorat nahi.' Galti kya hai?
answer: One food can have more than one nutrient; groundnut also has protein. Each nutrient needs its own test.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a classmate who was absent how the teacher tests foods for starch and for fat in class, and give one safety rule.
prompt_hi: Jo classmate absent tha, use samjhao ki class mein teacher khaane mein starch aur fat kaise test karte hain, aur ek safety rule bhi batao.
answer: Key ideas: starch: put a few drops of dilute iodine on the food; blue-black means starch. Fat: rub the food on paper and let it dry; an oily translucent patch means fat. Safety: do chemical tests only with a teacher and never eat tested food or taste chemicals.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: in the protein test your teacher did, what colour shows protein?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: teacher ne jo protein test kiya, usme kaunsa rang protein dikhata hai?
answer: Violet (purple).

subject: science
prompt_en: Match each disease to the missing nutrient: night blindness, goitre, anaemia, scurvy.
prompt_hi: Har bimari ko kami wale poshak tatva se milao: raatondhi (night blindness), ghenga (goitre), khoon ki kami (anaemia), scurvy.
answer: Night blindness: vitamin A. Goitre: iodine. Anaemia: iron. Scurvy: vitamin C.

subject: science
prompt_en: Long ago, sailors spent months at sea eating only dry biscuits and salted meat, with no fresh fruit. Predict which illness many of them got, and what would have prevented it.
prompt_hi: Bahut pehle naavik mahino samundar mein sirf sookhe biscuit aur namak lage meat pe rehte the, taaza phal bilkul nahi. Guess karo unme se kai logon ko kaunsi bimari hui, aur kya karne se bachte?
answer: Scurvy (bleeding gums, weakness) from lack of vitamin C; fresh fruits such as lemons, oranges or amla would have prevented it.

subject: science
prompt_en: Two children eat the same total amount daily. Child A eats only rice. Child B eats rice, dal, vegetables, fruit and milk. Predict who will be healthier after a few months, and why.
prompt_hi: Do bachche roz utna hi khaana khaate hain. Bachcha A sirf chawal khaata hai. Bachcha B chawal, dal, sabzi, phal aur doodh. Guess karo kuch mahino baad kaun zyada healthy hoga, aur kyon?
answer: Child B. Child A gets mostly carbohydrates and lacks proteins, vitamins, minerals and fibre, so may grow poorly, feel weak and develop deficiencies.

subject: science
prompt_en: In a dry year with little rain, a farmer in Rajasthan plants bajra in one field and rice in another. Predict which crop is more likely to do well.
prompt_hi: Kam baarish wale saal mein Rajasthan ka ek kisaan ek khet mein bajra aur doosre mein chawal lagata hai. Guess karo kaunsi fasal achhi hogi.
answer: Bajra; millets need much less water and tolerate heat and dry soil, while rice needs a lot of water.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why is iodised salt (salt with added iodine) used in most Indian homes?
prompt_hi: Zyada-tar Bharatiya gharon mein iodine wala namak kyon use hota hai?
answer: To prevent iodine deficiency, which causes goitre; the body needs iodine for the thyroid gland, and many foods and soils have too little of it.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare two breakfasts: a ragi dosa with chutney and a glass of milk, and a packet of chips with a cold drink. Which is closer to balanced, and why?
prompt_hi: Do naashte compare karo: ragi dosa chutney ke saath aur ek glass doodh, ya chips ka packet aur cold drink. Kaunsa balanced ke zyada kareeb hai, aur kyon?
answer: The ragi dosa and milk: it gives carbohydrates, protein, calcium and fibre. Chips and a cold drink give mostly fat, salt and sugar, with little protein, vitamins or fibre.

subject: science
prompt_en: Your friend often feels tired, looks pale and gets breathless while playing. A doctor finds she lacks iron. Suggest three foods she could eat more of.
prompt_hi: Tumhari dost aksar thaki rehti hai, peeli dikhti hai aur khelte hue saans phoolti hai. Doctor ko pata chala use iron ki kami hai. 3 khaane batao jo use zyada khaane chahiye.
answer: Any three: green leafy vegetables (palak, methi), jaggery, bajra or ragi, pulses and chana, dates, eggs or meat if she eats them; vitamin C foods like amla help the body absorb iron.

subject: science
prompt_en: Plan one balanced lunch for a family in your region using at least one millet. Name each food and the nutrient it mainly gives.
prompt_hi: Apne ilaake ke ek parivaar ke liye ek balanced lunch plan karo jisme kam se kam ek millet ho. Har khaana aur uska mukhya poshak tatva batao.
answer: Any balanced plan with a millet, e.g.: bajra roti (carbohydrate, iron, fibre), dal (protein), palak sabzi (vitamins, minerals, fibre), curd (protein, calcium), salad (vitamins, fibre), a little ghee (fat) and water.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw a table with three columns: nutrient, disease if missing, food that prevents it. Fill in rows for vitamin A, vitamin D and iron.
prompt_hi: 3 column wali table banao: poshak tatva, kami se bimari, bachane wala khaana. Vitamin A, vitamin D aur iron ki rows bharo.
answer: Vitamin A: night blindness: carrot, papaya, mango, green leafy vegetables. Vitamin D: rickets: sunlight, milk, eggs. Iron: anaemia: green leafy vegetables, jaggery, bajra, pulses.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu says: 'I eat five parathas with lots of butter every morning, so I'm eating a balanced diet.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Main roz subah bahut saare makkhan ke saath paanch parathe khaata hoon, isliye mera diet balanced hai.' Galti kya hai?
answer: A lot of food is not the same as balance: this is mostly carbohydrate and fat, lacking protein, vitamins, minerals and fibre, and too much fat can lead to obesity.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your grandparents why schools and the government are encouraging millets again.
prompt_hi: Apne daada-daadi ya naana-naani ko samjhao ki school aur sarkar phir se millets ko badhava kyon de rahe hain.
answer: Key ideas: millets like ragi, jowar and bajra are rich in fibre and minerals (ragi has calcium, bajra has iron); they need little water and grow in dry, poor soils; they are good for health and for farmers in dry areas; 2023 was the International Year of Millets.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: a child with soft, bent leg bones may lack which vitamin, and what free source helps the body make it?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: naram, mudi hui haddiyon wale bachche mein kis vitamin ki kami ho sakti hai, aur kaunsa muft source shareer ko ise banane mein madad karta hai?
answer: Vitamin D (the disease is rickets); sunlight on the skin.

subject: science
prompt_en: Pick three foods in your kitchen. Ask an adult or read the packet to find out where each came from.
prompt_hi: Apne kitchen ki 3 cheezein chuno. Kisi bade se poochh ke ya packet padh ke pata karo ki har ek kahan se aayi.
answer: Any three foods with a correct place of origin from a label or an adult, e.g. tea from Assam, apples from Himachal Pradesh, rice from Punjab.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: an apple from Himachal Pradesh travels by truck to Chennai, and a banana grows on a farm 20 km from Chennai. Which used more fuel to reach the Chennai market?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: Himachal ka seb truck se Chennai jaata hai, aur Chennai se 20 km door ke khet mein kela ugta hai. Chennai ki mandi tak pahunchne mein kisme zyada fuel laga?
answer: The apple; it travelled more than 2,000 km, while the banana travelled only about 20 km.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict what is needed to keep strawberries fresh on a long, hot journey from far away, and what that adds.
prompt_hi: Guess karo, door se lambe garam safar mein strawberry ko taaza rakhne ke liye kya chahiye, aur isse kya badhta hai?
answer: Refrigerated trucks or cold storage and special packaging; these use more energy, cost more and create more packaging waste.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why does food that travels a long way usually add more pollution?
prompt_hi: Jo khaana bahut door se aata hai, woh aam taur pe zyada pradooshan kyon badhata hai?
answer: Vehicles burn fuel such as diesel for the whole journey, so longer trips release more smoke and gases; cold storage on the way also uses energy.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare mangoes bought in May from the local mandi with mangoes bought in December that came from very far away. Which are local and seasonal, and what are their advantages?
prompt_hi: Mai mein local mandi se khareede aam aur December mein bahut door se aaye aam compare karo. Kaunse local aur mausami hain, aur unke kya fayde hain?
answer: The May mangoes are local and seasonal: fresher, usually cheaper, fewer food miles and they support local farmers.

subject: science
prompt_en: Your family's tea packet says 'Product of Assam'. If you live in Jaipur, are its food miles short or long? Why?
prompt_hi: Ghar ki chai ke packet pe likha hai 'Product of Assam'. Agar tum Jaipur mein rehte ho, toh iske food miles kam hain ya zyada? Kyon?
answer: Long; Assam is in the far north-east, well over 1,500 km from Jaipur, so the tea travels a long way.

subject: science
prompt_en: Your school wants to cut food miles for its mid-day meal. Suggest three practical ideas.
prompt_hi: Tumhara school mid-day meal ke food miles kam karna chahta hai. 3 practical idea batao.
answer: Any three: buy vegetables and grains from nearby farmers; use seasonal produce; grow a school kitchen garden; use local millets; reduce packaged foods.

subject: science
prompt_en: On a map of India, draw an arrow showing apples coming from Himachal Pradesh to Chennai, and another showing bananas coming from a farm near Chennai. Which arrow is longer, and what does arrow length stand for?
prompt_hi: India ke map pe ek teer banao jo Himachal se Chennai tak seb aate dikhaye, aur doosra jo Chennai ke paas ke khet se kele aate dikhaye. Kaunsa teer lamba hai, aur teer ki lambai kya dikhati hai?
answer: The apple arrow is much longer; arrow length stands for food miles (distance travelled).

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu says: 'Food miles are just the distance from the shop to my house, so my food miles are only 1 km.' Fix Golu's idea.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Food miles bas dukaan se mere ghar tak ki doori hai, isliye mere food miles sirf 1 km hain.' Golu ki soch theek karo.
answer: Food miles count the whole journey from the farm or factory to the plate; the 1 km from the shop is only the last small part.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your family why choosing local and seasonal fruit is good, and when it is still fine to buy food from far away.
prompt_hi: Apne parivaar ko samjhao ki local aur mausami phal chunna achha kyon hai, aur kab door se aaya khaana lena bhi theek hai.
answer: Key ideas: local and seasonal food has fewer food miles, needs less fuel and causes less pollution, is fresher and supports local farmers; it is fine to buy from far away when a food cannot be grown nearby and is needed for a balanced diet.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: give two problems caused when food travels very long distances.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: jab khaana bahut lambi doori tay karta hai, toh do samasyaayein batao.
answer: Any two: more fuel burnt and more air pollution; it loses freshness; it needs cold storage, packaging or preservatives; it can cost more.

subject: science
prompt_en: Name three materials a magnet attracts and three it does not.
prompt_hi: 3 materials batao jinhe magnet kheenchta hai aur 3 jinhe nahi.
answer: Attracts: iron, nickel, cobalt (and steels containing iron). Does not attract (any three): aluminium, copper, brass, plastic, wood, glass, paper, rubber.

subject: science
prompt_en: Before testing, predict: will a magnet pick up a piece of aluminium foil? An iron nail? A copper wire?
prompt_hi: Test karne se pehle guess karo: kya magnet aluminium foil uthayega? Lohe ki keel? Taambe ka taar?
answer: Only the iron nail; aluminium and copper are metals but they are not magnetic.
